hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

apprenticeship_location.description: The country where the child has started an apprenticeship, where relevant.

Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes, I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 19 and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

Since Alex is 19 and living at home with you, I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college anymore. He finished his A-levels last year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

**Is Alex registered with a government-sponsored careers service or with the armed services?**

This is important because if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either of these, Child Benefit can continue for up to 20 weeks. However, I notice Alex is 19, so I need to understand his current status.

- He lives at home with you
- He finished his A-levels last year and is not currently in approved education or training
- He is not working
- He is not registered with a careers service or the armed services

**One final question: Is Alex currently claiming any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?**

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid **you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

Child Benefit normally covers children under 16, but it can continue for children under 20 if they stay in approved education or training. Since Alex is 19 and finished his A-levels last year without continuing in approved education or training, he no longer meets the eligibility criteria.

The special provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks after leaving education (if registered with a careers service or armed services) only applies to 16 or 17 year olds, so this wouldn't apply to Alex at age 19.

If Alex's circumstances change - for example, if he decides to go to college, university, or begins approved training - you may become eligible again. If that happens, you would need to make a new claim.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
